source_columns: fdoc_yr, gdoc_yr, hdoc_yr, qdoc_yr, odoc_yr, pdoc_yr, tdoc_yr, rdoc_yr, ldoc_yr, b7intyr, wave
expression:
coalesce(
  1900 +
    coalesce(
      as.numeric(fdoc_yr),
      as.numeric(gdoc_yr),
      as.numeric(hdoc_yr),
      as.numeric(qdoc_yr),
      as.numeric(odoc_yr),
      as.numeric(pdoc_yr),
      as.numeric(tdoc_yr),
      as.numeric(rdoc_yr),
      as.numeric(ldoc_yr)
    ),
  as.numeric(b7intyr),
  recode_values(wave, "age16" ~ 1986, "child2004" ~ 2004)
)
notes: Per-row year. age16: completion year of Document F (the screen items), else the first dated document (G, H, Q, O, P, T, R, L); 245 rows with no dated document take 1986, the modal fieldwork year. child2004: interview year.

expression: as.character(bcsid)
notes: The cohort member's identifier (bcsid): a cohort member's age16 row and that cohort member's children in child2004 share it, so children of one parent (the cohort member, their mother or father) share an id; 2,846 cohort members have children in child2004, 1,761 of them two or more. The 222 twins of the age-16 sample cannot be linked to each other: the release records twin status (tc2) but no twin-pair identifier. Siblings share the cohort member's household and parent items (e.g. ses_household, maternal_education, maternal_employment).

expression: recode_values(wave, "age16" ~ "Cohort members", "child2004" ~ "Cohort members' children")
notes: Two separately recruited samples, split by the tidier's sweep files. 'Cohort members' (age16): the 1970 British Cohort Study birth cohort, people born in Britain on 5-11 April 1970 (with those born abroad in that week added at later sweeps), observed at 16 in 1986. 'Cohort members' children' (child2004): the co-resident natural or adopted children aged under 17 of a one-in-two sample of cohort members, recruited through them in the 2004 Parent and Child survey and given their own instruments. Each participant has one row, so the label is constant within participant.

expression: "General population"
notes: Nationally representative birth cohort of people born in Britain in one week of 1970, and their children in the 2004 Parent and Child survey (BCS70 user guides).

source_columns: resp, flag_o, flag_p, flag_t, bd7sex, wave
expression:
case_when(
  wave == "child2004" ~ recode_values(as.numeric(bd7sex), 2 ~ "Mother", 1 ~ "Father", default = "Unknown"),
  as.numeric(resp) == 1 ~ "Mother",
  as.numeric(resp) == 2 ~ "Father",
  as.numeric(resp) %in% 3:5 ~ "Other carer",
  as.numeric(resp) == 6 ~ "Both parents",
  as.numeric(flag_o) == 1 | as.numeric(flag_p) == 1 | as.numeric(flag_t) == 1 ~ "Unknown",
  .default = NA_character_
)
notes: age16: 'Status of respondent(s)' on the parental interview (resp, Document O, the main parent interview; the screen-time items are the teenager's own): mother figure = Mother, father figure = Father, mother and father = Both parents, other female, male or sex not known = Other carer (relationship not recorded). Unknown on 1,231 rows with Document O but no status and 1,055 rows with only the maternal self-completion or family follow-up form (Documents P and T, which record no respondent); NA on 976 rows with no 1986 parent document. child2004: the cohort member answered the parent interview and self-completion forms and is the child's natural or adoptive parent by design, so Mother when the cohort member is female and Father when male (bd7sex). Not carried.

case_when(
  wave == "age16" ~ 1900 +
    coalesce(
      as.numeric(fdoc_yr) + (as.numeric(fdoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12,
      as.numeric(gdoc_yr) + (as.numeric(gdoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12,
      as.numeric(hdoc_yr) + (as.numeric(hdoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12,
      as.numeric(qdoc_yr) + (as.numeric(qdoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12,
      as.numeric(odoc_yr) + (as.numeric(odoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12,
      as.numeric(pdoc_yr) + (as.numeric(pdoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12,
      as.numeric(tdoc_yr) + (as.numeric(tdoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12,
      as.numeric(rdoc_yr) + (as.numeric(rdoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12,
      as.numeric(ldoc_yr) + (as.numeric(ldoc_mt) - 0.5) / 12

Only how often the parent took away TV privileges or other treats as a punishment (2004, last three months), not a rule limiting amount or timing.

Only whether the family watched a video together in the last month (bd7video, child2004, cohort member's interview), a yes/no item. The 1986 leisure diary records who was present in each episode, but its co-presence code pools parents with other relatives ('2 or more relatives', 17% of television minutes) and is blank for 64% of television minutes, so the share of viewing with a parent cannot be isolated.
Only how often the cohort member (the parent) uses a computer at home and the internet (b7hpcuse, b7intqnt, child2004: daily to less than once a week), frequency items with no duration.

No depression scale: only single items (the Malaise item 'miserable or depressed', pd1.3 at age16 and b7mal03 at child2004, scored in fam_parent_distress; the Kessler item 'so depressed that nothing could cheer you up', b7k1) and whether the cohort member suffered from depression in the last year (b7dep12m), a history item.
No anxiety scale; only Malaise items on worry and sudden fear (pd1.5, pd1.12 at age16; b7mal05, b7mal12 at child2004), scored in fam_parent_distress.

The parent's own Malaise Inventory. age16: all 24 items of the maternal self-completion form (Document P, pd1.1-pd1.24; addressed to the mother, usually completed by her, the completer not recorded), asked with a three-point frequency response instead of yes/no: most of the time 2, some of the time 1, rarely or never 0; complete-case sum 0-48 (observed 0-46). The study's BD4MMAL sums answered items and equals this wherever all 24 are answered, so it is not used. child2004: the cohort member's own 9-item Malaise short form (b7mal02-b7mal21; yes 1, no 0), complete-case sum 0-9 (the study's BD7MAL counts yes over answered items and equals this wherever all nine are answered): the mother when the cohort member is female, else the responding father, whose partner was not asked. The four Kessler items (b7k1-b7k4, a partial K6) are not used. Forms differ by sweep; standardise within wave. Never carried.

local({
  codes <- cbind(as.character(b7xche2a), as.character(b7xche2b), as.character(b7xche2c), as.character(b7xche2d))
  codes[is.na(codes)] <- ""
  counted_code <- grepl("^[A-Z][0-9]", codes) & !grepl("^(F|R48|R62|L2|L30|J30|T78)", codes)
  counted <- rowSums(matrix(counted_code, nrow = nrow(codes))) > 0
  case_when(
    wave == "child2004" & as.numeric(b7pchea1) == 1 & counted ~ "Currently diagnosed",
    wave == "child2004" & as.numeric(b7pchea1) %in% 1:2 ~ "Never diagnosed",
    wave == "age16" & (as.numeric(rc3.6) %in% c(1, 6) | as.numeric(rc3.10) %in% c(1, 6)) ~ "Currently diagnosed",
    wave == "age16" & (as.numeric(rc3.6) == 2 | as.numeric(rc3.10) == 2) ~ "Previously diagnosed",
    wave == "age16" & as.numeric(rc3.6) == 4 & as.numeric(rc3.10) == 4 ~ "Never diagnosed"
  )
})
notes: child2004 (ages 1-16, parent interview): 'Does [child] have any longstanding physical, emotional or mental conditions that have been diagnosed by a health professional?' (b7pchea1; had or expected for at least 3 months), with the conditions written in and ICD-10-coded by the study (b7xche2a-b7xche2d). Yes with a counted code = Currently diagnosed; No, and Yes with only uncounted or uncoded conditions (171 rows), = Never diagnosed. Not counted: mental, behavioural and developmental codes (F, R48 dyslexia, R62 developmental delay), eczema and dermatitis (L2, L30), hay fever (J30) and allergy (T78); eye and ear conditions are counted. age16: Document R, completed by the community medical officer or school nurse from the examination, school medical records and the parental interview, 'Has this teenager ever had any of the following conditions?' for asthma (rc3.6) and a pathological heart condition (rc3.10): yes in the past 12 months on either = Currently diagnosed; otherwise yes before the past 12 months on either = Previously diagnosed; no never on both = Never diagnosed; age not known, not known and no form NA unless the other item places the child. Partial: the 2004 item asks about current conditions, so Never pools resolved conditions with never-diagnosed ones; age16 covers two conditions, with the past 12 months as proxy for current. The 2004 'ever had' health-problems card (b7pchl01-b7pchl07) names no health professional and is not used, nor are the other Document R conditions (eczema, hay fever, acute illnesses, enuresis, retardation, 'any other significant illness or disability').
